nodes.label: Operator runbook for the bulk tenant branding rollout (config shape, logo folder, colour/SEO field reference)
Service-role key must come from .env and never be committed — the runbook's only security instruction
branding-config.json contract: slug + app_name + logo/favicon paths + light/dark colour pairs + SEO meta
MOT and road-tax due-date backfill — randomises dates across overdue/upcoming so compliance alerts have data
Vehicle gallery backfill — inserts one vehicle_photos row per seeded make/model, skipping vehicles that already have photos
Bulk multi-tenant branding rollout — one JSON config drives palette, SEO and contact updates across many tenants
Logo/favicon upload to the company-logos storage bucket with timestamped filenames as cache-busting
Service-role client with autoRefreshToken/persistSession off, deliberately bypassing tenant RLS for cross-tenant writes
The tenants-row branding column family (primary/secondary/accent x light+dark, header_footer, logo_url, favicon_url, meta_title/description, app_name)
Bootstraps the tenant's 'site-settings' CMS page — the container the footer/logo/social CMS layer writes into
Point portal/booking/admin/web at the staging Supabase clone or back at production by rewriting each .env.local
Production keys are never hard-coded: first staging switch copies .env.local to .env.local.prod.bak, and 'prod' just restores that backup
Staging Supabase project ref ksmreaadhbirzakkxqrq — the constant that identifies 'not production'
Frees dev ports 3000-3005 before every dev server start, so no app ever falls through to an alternate port
lsof exits non-zero when nothing is listening — the empty catch is intentional, not a swallowed error
Seeds 100 vehicles chosen to be insurable under Bonzah, with generated UK-style plates, VINs and full mileage/deposit config
Bonzah underwriting exclusion list encoded as data: no Ferrari/Lamborghini/Bentley/Porsche etc., and per-model carve-outs (no Corvette, no Cybertruck)
Inserts in chunks of 25 to stay under PostgREST payload limits, reporting per-chunk instead of failing the whole batch
Registration/VIN generation is offset by the tenant's existing vehicle count so re-runs never collide on reg
Full demo dataset for the Bonzah tenant — branding, locations, fleet, customers, rentals, payments, fines, expenses, P&L
Re-runnable by design: cleanup deletes child tables before parents in a hand-ordered list before any insert
pnl_entries must be deleted by vehicle_id as well as tenant_id — trigger-created P&L rows can carry a null tenant_id
Only the 'Service' expense category is seeded because handle_vehicle_expense_pnl mirrors other categories into pnl_entries with the invalid category 'Expenses' (DB trigger bug)

Inline catalogue of the money-table CHECK constraints (payment_type, payment status, verification_status, ledger type/category, fine status/type/liability, pnl side/category and its three unique keys)
Bonzah brand profile — magenta palette, US locale (USD/miles/MM-DD-YYYY/America-New_York), Miami address, multi-location mode and per-day opening hours
Every seeded payment is mirrored as a Charge ledger entry plus a Payment entry when applied — the demo hand-builds the invariant the app's triggers normally maintain
Ledger seeding is deliberately skipped in main() — entries are treated as trigger-generated or non-critical for the demo
Generates sample PDF receipts with jsPDF and attaches them to MOCK-DATA expenses so the receipt preview/download UI is exercisable
receipt_url stores a bucket-relative path ({tenant}/mock-receipt-{id}.pdf) in expense-receipts, not a public URL — the UI signs it at read time
Borrows credentials by parsing apps/portal/.env.local directly instead of dotenv — couples the script to the portal app's env file layout
Seeds the same five template vehicles into EVERY tenant found, with reg plates prefixed from the tenant slug
Seeds a 30-vehicle UK-style fleet plus 1-3 vehicle_photos each into one hard-coded tenant id
Production Supabase URL and keys (anon in five scripts, service_role in two) are literal constants in committed source rather than env vars
Thin client for the staging-only sim-control edge function — list/shift/fire, the shared engine behind both the terminal harness and the DevPanel Time Machine
Two independent production guards: an exact-hostname sentinel that throws at import time, and sim-control itself 403ing off-staging
Compresses ~30 days of PAYG accrual on a staging rental into seconds by backdating the rental then re-firing the accrual cron
accrue-payg-charges posts at most maxDaysFor() days per dispatch, so a steady per-fire count is progress not a stall — drain the backlog, bound the loop, assert ledger state not counts
One-shot tenant provisioning from the onboarding sheet — fills the tenants row and (optionally) CMS copy, locations, FAQs, testimonials and extras for both portal and booking site
Idempotent by construction: tenants row updated in place, CMS sections upserted, and seed tables written only when the tenant has none
Strict by default — only real config data is written; --demo-content generates invented marketing copy that must be reviewed and never presented as factual claims
Derives a full light+dark brand palette from free-text branding input (hex codes or colour words), falling back to a slate+indigo default
lightenForDark floors lightness (and keeps saturation) so a brand colour never renders dark-on-dark for links and buttons in dark mode
Operator rules are never guessed: minimum_rental_age and deposit settings are written only when explicitly present in config, and absent hours leave tenant defaults alone
service_area drives all customer-facing prose/tagline/meta for multi-area operators while city/state stay split so the structured footer address still reads cleanly
US state abbreviation to state-name and IANA timezone map — how a sheet's 'FL' becomes tenants.timezone
Parses free-text opening hours ('24/7', '8am - 9pm') into the seven per-day enabled/open/close tenant columns
Parametrised generator for the 10 booking-site CMS pages — section keys and JSON shapes ported from update-cms-content.js because the booking site expects them exactly
Credential auto-discovery walks process.env then .env, .env.local, apps/portal/.env.local and apps/booking/.env.local
Notification branding regression harness — invokes eight notify-* edge functions with synthetic payloads to prove they use tenant branding instead of hardcoded values
TEST_TENANT_ID is optional on purpose — running without it exercises the default-branding fallback path, running with it proves tenant branding wins
Result parsing distinguishes 'simulated' from 'sent' per channel, so an unconfigured Resend/AWS environment reads as a pass rather than a silent no-op
Upserts every generated section into cms_page_sections for each existing CMS page, then publishes the page

Hard-coded registry of thirteen production tenants (Global Motion, FLEETVANA, AMG Roadside, Kedic, SD Rentals, Thomcell, All in One, DB Car Rentals, Jangram, RevTek, Vitalis, Ediberth) with their real phone/email/city/hours
Copy template leaks the first tenant's positioning: 'economy'/'Prius'/'Ford Fusions' and the literal SEO keyword 'car rental Nashville' are emitted for every tenant

The canonical booking-site section-key vocabulary (home_hero, service_highlights, booking_header, contact_info, fleet_hero, inclusions, promotions_hero, privacy_content, terms_content, site-settings logo/contact/social/footer)
Sets vehicles.photo_url from a make+model to Unsplash URL map
Matches on make/model only with no tenant_id filter, so a run rewrites the photo of every tenant's matching vehicle
Nuclear reset — deletes every row from ~50 tables including tenants and app_users

Hand-maintained foreign-key teardown order: reminders, notifications, money, fines, insurance, vehicle children, invoices, rentals, vehicles, customer children, customers, CMS, logs, settings, users, tenants last
Delete-all is expressed as neq on a sentinel uuid, falling back to created_at >= epoch for tables without an id column
auth.users survives the wipe and must be cleared by hand in the Supabase dashboard — the reset is not actually complete
sim-control edge function (staging-only time machine engine)
